newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European stocks smash records, look for more.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European stocks smash records, look for more.

text.p: European stock markets led by Britain, France and Germany ramapaged to new records on Wednesday, while the reinvigorated dollar again traded above 116 yen and around 1.80 marks.

The UK's FTSE 100 index was up more than 90 points to 4,990 points in mid-afternoon, charging further into record territory within grasp of the 5,000 hurdle. Banks contributed almost half of the FTSE's advance.

"It looks like there's nothing to stop us from reaching 5,000," said one trader, after the markets overcame the hurdles of jobs and public borrowing data in Britain and June consumer prices in the U.S.
"One is slightly at a loss for words," said Nick Knight, London-based investment strategist at the Japanese brokerage Nomura.
"It would not appear to be fundamentally justified but this is a very powerful move and it would be extremely rash to deny it...one has to be careful about writing it off as madness."

The market's strong gains came despite last week's quarter point interest rate rise by the Bank of England, making Britain the only major economy in Europe or the U.S. to be under the cosh of higher borrowing costs.
A sharp rise in sterling to 6-1/2 year highs against the German mark has proved especially problematic for big industrial companies that export to Europe.
U.S. blue chip stocks traded marginally higher at the market open on Wednesday while technology stocks rocketed up after solid results from computer chip firm Intel and the CPI data.
The Dow Jones industrial index rose more than 26 points and broke through 8,000 points in early trading.
"The CPI was a pleasant surprise," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co said. "The overall trend is up and the focus is on earnings expansion."

Germany's IBIS DAX stayed above 4,200 points in IBIS post-bourse computer dealings after the blue-chip index ended bourse trade above the psychologically important level. Firmer dollar and German debt price gains supported market.
Retailer Karstadt was up 20.90 marks at 662 marks on the outlook for restructuring despite expectations it may be dropped from the DAX in favour of Adidas.
French shares set a fresh all-time high after Wall Street opened higher and dealers said the 3,000 level on the CAC 40 index could be tested.
The dollar trading up towards 1.80 marks shrugged off a German government comment that there was no need to dramatise the foreign exchange situation.
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann told journalists after a cabinet meeting that Germany remained in close contact with its G7 partners about the foreign exchange developments.

"From Germany's point of view there is no reason to dramatise developments," Hausmann said, adding that the mark's current weakness against the dollar and the pound should be seen as a result of the strong economies in the U.S. and Britain.
He said the Group of Seven industrial nations said in February in Berlin that the appreciation of the mark had been fully corrected.
"Together with our G7 partners we are closely observing developments on foreign exchange markets," Hausmann said.
He said that Chancellor Helmut Kohl stressed at the cabinet meeting that the euro should be introduced on time in 1999 and that it would be a strong currency.
"Kohl stressed again in cabinet that the euro will come on time and the euro will be strong," Hausmann said.
He said the government believes speculation ahead of the planned launch of economic and monetary union (EMU) was affecting the foreign exchange markets. CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 115.98 yen and 1.7990 marks compared with 115.74 yen and 1.8013 marks in late trading on Tuesday. STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 87.6 points at 4,986.9.
FRANKFURT - The IBIS DAX index was up 76.33 points at 4,216.01.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 40.15 points at 2,990.85.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $319.50, unchanged from the morning fixing. Silver was at $4.32, unchanged from the opening.
